metadata.description: Authoritative ground-truth landslide inventory covering four distinct physiographic zones of India. Compiled strictly from documented scientific and government sources. Approximate points are explicitly distinguished from verified polygons.
metadata.attribution_policy: All data referenced under official government and open-access scientific licenses (NDSAP, Copernicus EMS Open Access, NASA Open Data CC0).

western_himalayas.monitoring_context: Deep glacial valleys, steep rock faces, snow/moraine coverage, flash flood risk

primary_event.source_reference: Copernicus EMS Activation EMSR501; Geological Survey of India Post-Disaster Geotechnical Report (Feb 2021); Shugar et al., Science 373(6552), 2021

eastern_himalayas.physiographic_zone: Steep Sub-Tropical to Alpine Montane Slopes
eastern_himalayas.monitoring_context: Dense montane evergreen forests, deeply incised gorges, high monsoonal rainfall, extreme cloud persistence

primary_event.event_name: South Lhonak Glacial Lake Outburst & Teesta Valley Slopes
primary_event.source_name: ISRO National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) / NASA GLC
primary_event.source_reference: ISRO NRSC Report on Sikkim Flood Disaster (Oct 2023); NASA GLC ID 15024; Central Water Commission Technical Bulletin
primary_event.source_license: ISRO Open Access for Research / NASA Public Domain
primary_event.data_limitation_note: ISRO published high-resolution flood and landslide inundation maps, but the raw vector shapefile requires restricted portal authentication. Event point and valley bounds are verified from official technical reports, but fine boundary polygons are not freely downloadable in raw vector format.

verified_positive_patches.label: POSITIVE
verified_positive_patches.ground_truth_evidence: Teesta III dam breach zone and flank slope washouts documented in NRSC bulletin

verified_positive_patches.label: POSITIVE
verified_positive_patches.ground_truth_evidence: Lachen river toe erosion and massive slope collapse

verified_negative_control_patches.label: NEGATIVE
verified_negative_control_patches.stability_evidence: Stable forested ridge south of Gangtok outside Teesta flash flood basin

verified_negative_control_patches.label: NEGATIVE
verified_negative_control_patches.stability_evidence: Undisturbed temperate forest sanctuary with 100% stable canopy between Sept and Oct 2023

unverified_candidate_patches.label: UNVERIFIED
unverified_candidate_patches.reason: High altitude (5200m) glaciated moraine with permafrost and dynamic seasonal ice melt making optical distinction from pure mass wasting ambiguous without ground sensor confirmation

northern_western_ghats.monitoring_context: Terraced lava plateaus, red lateritic soils, high seasonal monsoon downpours, seasonal deciduous vegetation

primary_event.event_name: Taliye Village Debris Flow & Mahabaleshwar Escarpment
primary_event.source_name: Geological Survey of India (GSI) / NASA GLC
primary_event.source_reference: GSI Geotechnical Report on Catastrophic Slope Failure at Taliye, Mahad Taluk, Raigad (Aug 2021); NASA GLC ID 13890
primary_event.source_license: Government of India NDSAP / NASA Public Domain
primary_event.data_limitation_note: GSI field teams surveyed the crown, scarp and deposition toe using handheld GPS. While the exact crown coordinates and physical dimensions (150m width, 700m runout) are published, an authoritative vector polygon was never distributed via an open shapefile repository.

verified_positive_patches.label: POSITIVE
verified_positive_patches.ground_truth_evidence: GSI GPS surveyed crown and entire debris runout path over Taliye settlement

verified_negative_control_patches.label: NEGATIVE

verified_negative_control_patches.label: NEGATIVE
verified_negative_control_patches.stability_evidence: Flat agricultural valley floor confirmed unaffected by GSI district damage assessment
